text:
A: Hello! Greta! Finally. Hi!
B: Hi. Yes, finally. You're the moka pot.
A: Ha! Everybody says this today. I'm Marisol, Leyton. The moka pot is very famous now.
B: It should be. Is it a real Bialetti or a copy?
A: Real one! My sister brought it, eight years old. You know coffee?
B: I'm a snob, to be honest. Most coffee in this country is terrible. Big milky things with syrup.
A: Thank you! Hot brown water. I told Kerry and she said she drinks instant from Aldi and she said sorry. Bless her.
B: She apologised to you?
A: She apologised! I said I forgive you. So, Greta, where are you from originally? Not Peterborough, I think.
B: Lithuania. Panevėžys. I came at twenty. Fourteen years now.
A: Twenty! I came at twenty-two, from Colombia. Pereira, the coffee region, that's why the coffee.
B: Ah, that explains it. What did you do when you came?
A: Cleaning offices at night, in the City. Ten until five. My English was so bad, I just smiled. Everybody thought I was very happy.
B: I did nights in a food packing factory. Chicken, mostly. And I was doing a design course in the day, part-time, four years. I don't think I slept for four years.
A: Ay, four years. That's hard. But look, now you're a designer.
B: Part-time designer, for a man who likes everything big and red. So, sort of.
A: Bueno, sort of is still something. I was cleaning, now I manage twenty-two people. You start where you start.
B: Yes. That's true. Sometimes I think I'm still on the night shift in my head, you know?
A: I understand. Me also, sometimes. And people here, they ask, are you British now, are you Colombian, and I say I'm a Londoner who eats arepas.
B: I don't know what I am. In Lithuania they say I'm English now. Here they ask where I'm from every time I speak.
A: Every time! At the till, a customer says, oh, lovely accent, where from? I say Walthamstow.
B: Ha. That's good. I'll use that. Peterborough, Orton Goldhay.
A: Exactly! Do you go back?
B: Once or twice a year. I hate flying, I take something. You?
A: December, if head office lets me. My mum is getting older, so, you know.
B: Yes. I know. My grandmother died in the lockdown and I didn't go. I still think about it.
A: Ay, Greta. I'm sorry. That's a heavy thing to carry.
B: It's fine. Sorry, I don't usually say that to people.
A: No, no, it's okay. It's the same worry, all of us far away. Okay, your cardigan, the yellow, I love it. Where is it from?
B: Vinted. Eight pounds. Everything I own is from Vinted or a dead person's wardrobe.
